title: Regression Line Anatomy
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Hover over or click the five numbered parts of a fitted regression line (intercept, slope, predicted value, actual value, and residual) to read what each one means and see its value for ten students.

educational.topic: Parts of a regression line and its equation
learningObjectives: Students will be able to identify the intercept, slope, predicted value, actual value, and residual on a regression plot and in the regression equation.
prerequisites: Slope and y-intercept of a line
Mean of a set of numbers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Labeled diagram with hover and click to reveal, plus a hide-the-names self-test
keyQuestions: Which number in the equation tells you how steep the line is?
Why is the predicted value always on the line while the actual value usually is not?
What does a positive residual say about the model's prediction for that student?
commonMisconceptions: The residual is the shortest (perpendicular) distance from a point to the line (it is the vertical distance).
The intercept is where the line crosses the x-axis (it is where the line crosses the y-axis, at x = 0).
The regression line must pass through the data points (it usually passes through none of them).
A positive residual means the model predicted too high (the actual value is above the prediction, so the model predicted too low).
assessmentOpportunities: Given an unlabeled scatter plot with a regression line and its equation, students label the intercept, the slope triangle, one predicted value, one actual value, and the residual between them, and state the sign of that residual.
